scope: Retire post-NGE Beast Master identity, player-owned Beast combat XP and level progression, trainer grants, live-conversion reattachment, expertise arithmetic, persisted known-skill state, the exact seven-row player Beast-family helper surface, Shield Master/bodyguard buffs, and all inherited player damage redirection while Publish 14.1 Creature Handler tame/control runtime and retained later-content NPC, display, conversation, asset, template, and data content continue to load.

findings: Pinned Publish 14.1 Core3 has no Beast Master, incubator, expertise_bm_, or bm_* player runtime in its server and script gameplay trees.
Publish 14.1 creature pets are tamed, persisted, called, and controlled through Creature Handler skill modifiers and the pet control device lifecycle.
The current NGE source retains Beast Master data and NPC-capable scripts for compatibility, but those assets must not establish player progression or combat authority.
The retirement boundary is player-only; later-content NPC creatures and retained object/data loading are not deleted.

The retained generated Beast Master trainer and live-conversion script formed two bypasses around the original retirement boundary: one could persist Beast abilities and the other could reattach the retired player script.

Retained Beast AI and incubation content can use authored table, station, power, and incubation values, but no player Beast Master expertise or reverse-engineered Beast skill modifier may alter those values.

The production combat-XP fallback could still call Beast XP and level progression for a stale player-owned NGE Beast even after player Beast Master identity, creation, login, and commands were retired.
The shared Beast XP and level entrypoints now reject only Beasts mastered by a real player, so retained NPC, unowned, and invulnerable barn-display Beast content remains available.

The retained NGE Beast Master protection family has exactly three effect mappings and three buff rows: Shield Master applies a timed player/pet pair and bodyguard applies a persistent master redirect. Its specialized handlers write the shared damage_redirect state, and the inherited combat consumer also accepts later saber-intercept, Spy hologram, and battlefield-vehicle writers for players.

Pinned Core3 has no Shield Master/bodyguard mapping, damage_redirect state, or directDamageToDifferentTarget consumer. Exact player-only buff admission and lifecycle cleanup, player and player-master handler guards, and cleanup before the single inherited player consumer now retire every player damage-redirection path while retaining all data and non-player encounter behavior.

The retained Beast-family helper surface has exactly three bmBeastFamily mappings, seven persistent bm_player_buff rows, seven mapping uses, and seven direct player_beastmaster callbacks. Standard bm_ action admission and login group cleanup were already retired, but queued direct callbacks and the family add handler could still bypass the standard combat gate or propagate state between a player and a player-owned NGE Beast. Exact player admission and lifecycle cleanup, all seven direct callback guards, and the add handler's player and player-owned-Beast guards now close that residual path while every row, remove cleanup, unowned/NPC Beast behavior, and later pet-target content remain available.
